issues.legal_issue: Relatives listed together within a single succession entry inherit equally, and their order within that entry does not create a preference based on sex or numbering.
material_facts: A Hindu widow died intestate, leaving no issue or lineal descendants.
The property at issue was treated as property devolving through her deceased husband.
The surviving relatives in dispute were three of her husband's brothers and his sister, listed together within one entry of the relevant succession classification.
issues.conclusion: The brothers and sister succeeded jointly in equal shares; the numerals preceding their descriptions did not give the brothers preference.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 15 and 16, Rule 3, the succession to a female Hindu's property devolving upon her husband's heirs follows the order and rules that would have applied to the husband's property under sections 8 to 11. Sections 9 and 11 provide for preference between entries and equal division among heirs in the same Class II entry. The Court held that the numerals within an entry did not make separate entries or establish preference, consistent with the Act's scheme of equal treatment of male and female heirs. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.female_intestate_succession_dispute: The dispute concerns succession to the estate of a woman who died without a will.
predicates.property_devolves_through_husband: The property passes to relatives through the woman's deceased husband.
predicates.claimants_in_same_priority_group: The competing relatives are listed together within one succession group.
predicates.coheirs_share_equally: The relatives in that group inherit simultaneously in equal shares.

issues.definition: When a succession dispute concerns a woman's intestate estate, the property passes through her deceased husband, and the competing relatives are in the same priority group, those relatives inherit simultaneously in equal shares.
